paragraphs: Start with the conditions that shape every other garden decision. Look up a U.S. ZIP code or enter a known growing zone, then understand the winter-temperature range behind that result. Use it to narrow plant choices before buying seeds, perennials or shrubs.

A hardiness zone is a starting point, not a complete planting forecast. Pair it with your garden’s sun, drainage and local frost guidance. Save your zone so the connected Perennial tools and My Garden dashboard can work from the same growing context.
tool-zone.saveNote: Save your growing-zone result on this device.

paragraphs: Turn an idea into a layout you can inspect before moving soil or buying materials. Set the garden dimensions, place beds and growing areas, and organize plants, paths, containers and structures in a drawing that reflects the space you actually have.

Compare mature plant spread, companion relationships, shade and irrigation reach while you revise. Start with one bed or plan a larger project; then save a named layout to reopen later. Your saved plans also appear in My Garden, keeping the drawing connected to your wider garden records.
garden-planner.saveNote: Use Save for a named layout; Export creates a portable copy.

paragraphs: Bring measurements to the shopping decision. Enter the dimensions and depth for your project to estimate the soil, compost or mulch involved. Explore spacing and planting quantities without relying on a rough guess made while standing in a store aisle.

Change one measurement at a time to compare options for a bed or container project. Treat the results as planning estimates, then check the bag size, product coverage and site conditions before ordering. The goal is a clearer materials list and fewer avoidable shortages or surplus supplies.
tool-calc.saveNote: Keep your measurements and check product coverage before purchasing.

paragraphs: Look at the relationships within a planting plan, not just a list of plants you like. Search for a crop or garden plant to review possible companions, neutral neighbors and combinations that deserve extra space or closer attention.

Use the explanations to think about light, mature size, airflow and the growing conditions each plant needs. Companion planting is one planning aid rather than a promise of pest control or better yields. Save useful combinations, then bring those ideas into a layout that leaves room for the plants to grow.
tool-companion.saveNote: Save useful companion ideas to revisit through My Garden.

paragraphs: Turn the season into a manageable set of decisions. Review planting, maintenance and harvest tasks by growing context, then focus on the work that belongs in the current week or month instead of trying to tackle the entire garden at once.

Use the calendar alongside what you can actually observe outdoors. Weather, soil readiness and the needs of a particular crop can change the best date for a task. Keep your preferences consistent with My Garden, and use the Journal when you want a record of what you completed and how the garden responded.
tool-calendar.saveNote: Seasonal preferences stay in this browser; local conditions still matter.

paragraphs: Build a better garden-health question with several views of the same problem. Add a whole-plant photo, a close-up and other relevant evidence, then combine visible symptoms with growing conditions. Image-quality feedback helps you see when a clearer reference photo would be useful.

The current tool screens observations and visual cues to narrow possible plant, pest or disease matches. It is not a definitive AI identification or a substitute for Extension verification. Compare the explanations and trusted references before treating a plant, then save the report to follow the issue through My Garden.
plant-identifier.saveNote: Save observations and reports; full uploaded photos are not stored in saved reports.

paragraphs: Decide what to look for before you pick. Choose a crop and compare its maturity signs with the color, size, texture and other observations in your own garden. Review practical guidance for timing the harvest, handling produce and deciding when to check again.

A readiness check is most useful when it becomes part of a record. Note the variety and the signs you observed, then use Harvest Records to track the amount, quality and storage outcome. Over a season, that history can help you recognize what works for your garden and kitchen.
tool-harvest.saveNote: Save a harvest check, then record actual yields in Harvest Records.

paragraphs: Move from an unfamiliar plant name or gardening term to a useful reference. Search more than 2,700 plant records, botanical names, synonyms and garden vocabulary. Explore source-backed care information where it is available, with pronunciation and voice search on supported browsers.

Keep the records and references you want to return to in My Library. The Top 100 Gardening Books collection adds a separate reading path, with ranked editorial selections, practical uses and full book guides. Plant research, saved records and longer reading each have a clear place to begin.
garden-library.saveNote: Saved plants, terms, notes and book lists stay in this browser.

paragraphs: Follow a crop from the seed packet to transplant day. Organize seed inventory, sowing rounds, trays and cells, then record germination, potting-up and the next steps each batch needs. The tool is built for keeping several plantings understandable at the same time.

Plan repeat sowings so you can think beyond a single planting date. Check the active trays and due tasks before starting another batch, and record what happened rather than relying on memory. Saved seed and tray information feeds into My Garden alongside your other growing activity.
seed-starting.saveNote: Save your seed, tray and succession records on this device.

paragraphs: Give everyday garden work a useful history. Record watering, feeding, soil amendments, observations, treatments and follow-up tasks in one place. A short entry made when something happens can be more useful later than trying to reconstruct the whole season from memory.

Use the Journal to connect an action with what happened next: a change in watering, a new amendment or a plant that recovered slowly. Keep observations specific and add follow-up dates where useful. Your saved activity appears in My Garden, making it easier to return to the work that still needs attention.
garden-journal.saveNote: Save each entry; your journal remains private to this browser.

paragraphs: Measure what the garden gives back. Record harvest dates, crops, varieties, quantities, quality and storage details so the productive side of the garden has a history of its own. Keep a few beds or a larger mixed garden understandable over the season.

Review crop totals and compare seasons to support the next planting plan. The numbers do not need to be perfect to become useful: consistent units and honest observations make the record easier to interpret. Pair these entries with Harvest Checker when you want to remember the maturity signs behind a successful harvest.
harvest-records.saveNote: Save actual harvest records here; readiness guidance lives in Harvest Checker.

paragraphs: Check what you already own before adding another item to the cart. Organize supplies, low-stock items, shopping and wish lists, purchases and a garden budget. Keep the practical side of growing connected to the space and projects you are planning.

Use the inventory to spot duplicate purchases and turn an upcoming job into a more deliberate shopping list. Record costs as purchases happen so you can review spending alongside the season’s plans and results. Saved inventory and budget information is available through My Garden on the same device.
garden-inventory.saveNote: Save inventory and spending records in this browser.

paragraphs: Start with a garden name, growing zone and location label, then save your profile. My Garden brings together the records already saved by the connected tools, giving your garden a home without making an account a requirement.

Return here to review layouts, saved plants, seed activity, journal entries, harvests and garden-health reports. Save your work inside each tool first so it can appear on the dashboard. This version uses the current browser: it does not automatically sync to a different phone, computer or browser.
my-garden.saveNote: No account needed. Save in each tool; keep exports as backups where available.
